title: A typed title caret follows the letters as they are typed
goal: When a title types its words in (Command Line), the caret waits at the end of where the finished words will be, so for most of the entrance it floats in empty space to the right of the few letters on screen. It should sit right after the last letter typed, then blink after the words once they are all in.
notes: Seen 2026-11-21 in task keynote-clean-soft-gradient-glass-kinetic-bold-t: queue/audits/2026-11-21-title-redesign-old-new.png, Command Line row, 400 ms shows "Sh" with the caret about eight letters to the right, 700 ms "Ship fas" with the caret a word away; the old Tech Terminal row shows the same with "Yo". Frames come from PHOTONZ_REEL=1 PHOTONZ_REDESIGN_PHASE=after PHOTONZ_REDESIGN_DIR=/tmp/redesign Scripts/test.sh --filter TitleRedesignReel (after/terminal-400.png). The caret is a box after the words in a row stack (TitleSet.swift terminal(), Prompt row); the typewriter reveal hides letters without changing the row layout, so the caret keeps the full words width. TitleSetTests.cursorFollowsTheWords covers only the held state.
acceptance: At every frame of a typewriter entrance the caret left edge is within one letter width of the right edge of the ink typed so far
Once every letter is in, the caret waits after the words and blinks while the title holds, as today
The Command Line title-set walk still passes, and its contact sheet frames at 400 and 700 ms show the caret against the letters
